THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 10.06.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 MACA NO. 2873 OF 2008 Santhosh Pillai vs Chandran Pillai on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39897949/
1  2  2025:KER:40441  JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant in O.P (MV) No.997 of 2002 on the file of the IInd Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Kollam challenging the liability of the respondents to indemnify the insured.

entities.text: IInd Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Kollam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The respondents herein are the respondents before the tribunal.

2. According to the appellants/claimants, on 27.02.2002 at about 10.00 am, while the petitioner was pillion riding on a motorcycle, when he reached near Chathinamkulam junction, the motorcycle ran upon a hump.
As a result of which the motorcycle capsized and the appellant was thrown away and sustained severe injuries.
The claimant approached the tribunal claiming a total compensation of 3,00,000/-.
3. Before the tribunal, respondents 1 -3 are the driver, owner and the insurer of the offending motorcycle respectively.

Respondent 3 entered appearance and filed a written statement admitting the policy coverage for the vehicle KL1C/854 but denying the liability under the policy as it is an "Act only Policy" which does not cover the pillion rider.
Exts A1 to A9 were marked on the side MACA NO. 2873 OF 2008 2025:KER:40441 of the petitioner and no oral evidence was adduced on both the sides.
The third respondent was exonerated from the liability before the tribunal.

The Tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record, awarded a sum of 1,07,576/- as compensation under different heads with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization, against the 1st and 2nd respondent with costs.
Challenging the award exonerating the 3rd respondent insurer by the tribunal, the claimants have come up with this appeal.

4. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellant/claimant and the learned senior standing counsel appearing for the insurance company.
5.

The learned counsel appearing for the appellant submitted that along with the appeal, he had produced the copy of the policy wherein the additional premium was paid by the insured towards personal accident coverage.

Hence, the insurance company cannot be exonerated from the liability,
though the policy was an act only policy.

6. On the other hand, the learned senior standing counsel appearing for the insurance company submitted that the policy MACA NO. 2873 OF 2008 2025:KER:40441 being an act only policy, the personal accident coverage was to the rider of the vehicle and not for the pillion rider.

Admittedly,
the claimant herein was a pillion rider.
7. On perusal of the copy of the policy produced, it is seen that the premium has been paid for one person towards personal accident.
If that be so, the premium of policy will be applicable only for the rider of the motorcycle and not for the pillion rider.

The learned counsel for the appellant submitted Santhosh Pillai vs Chandran Pillai on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39897949/
2

entities.text: Santhosh Pillai vs Chandran Pillai on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: that additional premium for personal accident is given for a passenger and not for a rider.

However,
I do not find any merit in the said argument, since the policy is only an act only policy and the personal accident coverage can only be for the owner/rider of the vehicle.
I find that the pillion rider is not entitled to any compensation from the insurer.
Therefore, I do not find any reason to interfere with the award passed by the tribunal exonerating the insurance company from the liability.
Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed.

Sd/-
